theater: 淮南西部順昌柘皋戰線

battle.name: 柘皋之戰
battle.theater: 淮南西部順昌柘皋戰線
battle.brief: 紹興十一年正月，金元帥完顏宗弼率大軍南侵，圍淮西制置使劉錡所守的順昌。劉錡以霹靂砲與強弩擊退攻城器械，夜焚敵營，迫金軍退屯柘皋；追兵隨即攜攻城砲逼近，以砲火覆蓋敵營，再以步騎火攻衝入。卡面的配重式長臂砲同宋軍攻城砲同類而機構相異。此役後金軍北撤，促成十一月《紹興和議》。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰的兩方是南宋淮西軍與金朝河南軍。南渡之後，淮上的指揮權並不統一：淮西一路歸淮西制置使劉錡，駐軍順昌府；淮東一路歸江淮招討使張俊，兩軍分屬不同樞府與宣撫司，糧餉調度與援兵調度都要經臨安朝廷轉手，臨陣遇事往往各行其是。劉錡自紹興九年到鎮，第一件事不是擴軍而是整頓：汰老弱、核軍籍、修城濬壕、儲糧草、打造攻城與守城的器械，又在士卒面上刺字，編成名為「八字軍」的隊伍。其部以淮北降附的散兵、招募的鄉兵為主，步卒為骨幹，弩手與砲手另編，騎兵數量有限。器械方面，宋軍自帶雲梯、衝車、攻城砲、霹靂砲，攻防兩用，不依賴臨時徵發。金方以完顏宗弼為河南元帥，統中軍自河南、壽春一線南下，麾下是女真猛安謀克、契丹與漢軍混編的騎兵大軍，糧食由河北、山東與河南轉運，援軍可沿淮河北岸南北移動。宗弼以下另有留守淮北的將領，韓常便是其中之一，後來正是他代表金朝赴宋議和。柘皋在淮河北岸、合肥與滁州之間的大道上，是金軍由河南進入淮南的必經之地，也是宋軍在淮北最突出的一處據點，雙方在此都沒有退路。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Southern Song's Huaiwest army and the Jin armies out of Henan. After the court moved south the command on the Huai was not unified at all: the Huaiwest line belonged to Liu Qi, Military Commissioner for Huaiwest, who sat at Shunchang prefecture, while the Huai east line belonged to Zhang Jun, Inspector-General of the Jiang and Huai. The two armies sat under different military commissions and pacification offices, and the movement of grain and of reinforcements had to be relayed through the court at Lin'an, so that in contact each tended to act on his own judgement. When Liu Qi took command in the ninth year of Shaoxing (1139) his first business was not expansion but reform: he dismissed the old and the weak, checked the rolls, repaired the walls and dug the ditches, stored grain, and had the tools for siege and defence built; he also had characters tattooed on his men and organized the unit that came to be called the Eight-Character Army. His troops were mostly disbanded men from the north and villagers recruited locally, with infantry as the backbone, crossbowmen and artillery crews listed separately, and very few horsemen. In the matter of equipment the Song army brought its own scaling ladders, battering rams, throwing engines and thunder bombs, usable for attack and for defence alike, and did not depend on hastily levied material. On the Jin side Wanyan Zongbi acted as Marshal of Henan and led the central host down from Henan and from the Shouchun line; under him marched the great body of cavalry mixed from Jurchen meng'an mouke, Khitan and Han troops, fed from Hebei, Shandong and Henan, with reinforcements able to move north and south along the north bank of the Huai. Beneath Zongbi there were also generals left to hold the north bank, and Han Chang was one of them; it was Han Chang who later came south to negotiate for the Jin. Zhegao stood on the north bank of the Huai, on the great road between Hefei and Chuzhou. It was the road the Jin armies had to take to pass from Henan into the south of the river, and at the same time the most advanced post the Song held on the north bank, so neither side could afford to give way here.
people: 核心人物是劉錡，字信叔，福建南安人，生於元祐三年（一○九八），卒於紹興十二年（一一四二），年四十五。他自紹興九年出任淮西制置使、駐順昌，任內做的第一件事是整軍：汰老弱、核軍籍、修城濬壕、儲糧草，並在士卒面上刺「赤心報國，誓殺金賊」八字，軍中號為「八字軍」。金兵南下時，他以孤軍當大敵，事前已遣人拆毀淮南諸渡口的橋梁、焚燒敵軍屯於淮上的舟楫，切斷渡河與糧道，又屢次派斥候偵知金軍的虛實與集結時機。順昌被圍之後，他用霹靂砲震嚇敵騎、以勁弩齊射封住城根的攻城器械，又放出被俘的敵探，假報「夜劫寨」之期，使金軍主帥移營就範，宋軍趁夜縱火衝營，敵人自相踐踏，軍心大潰。破圍之後他不停追擊，直抵柘皋，焚金軍營壘，斬獲甚眾。金方主帥完顏宗弼是金朝宗室元帥，紹興十年（一一四○）曾率軍攻陷洛陽，一一四一年統河南軍南侵，志在打通淮南、逼迫南宋就範，卻在順昌與柘皋連折兵力，攻勢為之中止。朝廷另一面，主和的秦檜與湯思退同主戰的趙鼎、張浚意見相持，前線的勝負直接變成和談桌上的籌碼：紹興十一年（一一四一年）十月金遣韓常、張通古南下議和，十一月《紹興和議》成立，劉錡打下的戰果成了議桌上最硬的價碼。事後主和派不能容他，紹興十二年劉錡被罷兵權，改知荊州軍府事，後移湖南，旋以疾卒於潭州任上。
peopleEn: The central figure is Liu Qi, courtesy name Xinshu, a native of Nan'an in Fujian, born in the third year of Yuanyou (1098) and dead in the twelfth year of Shaoxing (1142) at the age of forty-five. He took up the post of Military Commissioner for Huaiwest and sat at Shunchang from the ninth year of Shaoxing (1139), and the first thing he did there was to reform the army: dismissing the old and the weak, checking the rolls, repairing the walls and moats, storing grain, and tattooing on his men the eight characters 'loyal heart to serve the country, sworn to kill the Jin', which gave the unit the name Eight-Character Army. When the Jin troops moved south he met a great host with a lone command, and he had already sent men to tear down the bridges at the crossings on the Huai and to burn the enemy's boats moored on the river, cutting the routes of crossing and supply, and he sent out scouts again and again to learn the strength of the Jin army and the moment of its concentration. Once Shunchang was surrounded he used the thunder bomb to shake the enemy cavalry and massed his heavy crossbows to seal off the siege engines working at the foot of the wall; he also released captured enemy scouts with false news of a night raid on the camp, so that the Jin commander shifted his camp to meet it, and the Song then fired the camp in the dark, the enemy trampling itself in the confusion. Having broken the siege he did not stop but pursued, carried the fight to Zhegao, and burned the Jin camps, taking a great many heads and prisoners. On the Jin side the commander in chief was Wanyan Zongbi, a prince of the Jin house and its marshal, who had taken Luoyang in the tenth year of Shaoxing (1140) and who in 1141 led the Henan armies south with the object of opening the way across the Huai and forcing the Song court to come to terms; he lost men in two actions in a row, at Shunchang and at Zhegao, and his offensive was checked. On the court's side, the advocates of peace, Qin Hui and Tang Si-tui, and the advocates of war, Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun, were deadlocked, and the fortunes of the front line became the currency of the peace table: in the tenth month of Shaoxing 11 (1141) the Jin sent Han Chang and Zhang Tonggu down to talk, in the eleventh month the Treaty of Shaoxing was concluded, and the results Liu Qi had won by force were the hardest bargaining chip on the table. Afterwards the party of peace could not leave him in place; in the twelfth year of Shaoxing Liu Qi was stripped of his command, made Military Commissioner of Jinghu, and later transferred to Hunan, where he died of illness at Tanzhou in the same year.
kits: 這件配重投石車在宋金之際的位置要分兩層講：功能上它是攻城的主幹，機構上它卻不是十二世紀中土的制式。先講功能：北宋《武經總要》所載的攻城砲（砲石車、霹靂車）是橫臂人力挽索式，靠百餘人同時挽索把石彈拋出，發石數十斤；劉錡在順昌與柘皋兩段用到的攻城器械正係這一類，配以霹靂砲、雲梯與衝車。再講機構：配重式的長臂投石車是十二世紀初地中海世界（拜占庭、十字軍國家、義大利城邦）的新器械，靠長臂下懸的配重下墜把石彈拋出，拋程更遠、落點更準；就中土而言，這種配重砲要到十三世紀蒙古軍帶中亞工匠東來、以「回回砲」之名出現，襄陽攻城（一二六八年至一二七三年）才大顯威力，一一四一年的順昌與柘皋不見其蹤。所以這件卡面兵器在本役的位置是「同類而異制」：它代表的拋石攻城邏輯——以弧線越過城頭、把石頭砸在城根的器械群與人群上——正是宋軍攻城砲在柘皋做的事，只不過實際發射者是橫臂挽索砲，而卡面這具配重砲留在地中海世界的城牆下。兩者可以並置比較的地方還有一點：配重砲只靠數人操縱，宋式挽索砲卻要上百人同時用力，後者的發射間隔、人力補充同攻城節奏都因此更慢——工程上，誰決定節奏，誰就決定攻城窗口的長短。除投石車外，宋軍尚備強弩與勁弩、長弓、長槍、刀、藤牌，攻城另有雲梯、衝車與蒙牛皮的攻城器，守城備擂木、滾木與拒馬；金軍攻城同樣備砲與雲梯，並以大量騎兵繞城掠糧、遮斷援兵。宋軍的馬匹主要用於偵察、追擊與傳令，糧秣多靠淮河船運與沿途州縣徵發，砲、弩等重件則靠牛車、騾車與人力搬運。
kitsEn: The place of this counterweight trebuchet in the Song and Jin armies of the time has to be taken in two parts. In function it was the mainstay of siege work; in mechanism it was not the standard instrument of mid-twelfth-century China. On the function: the attacking engines described in the Northern Song military manual, the Wujing Zongyao, under the names pao-shiche and pili-che, were of the traction type, with a transverse arm hauled by a hundred men or more working the ropes together to throw a stone of several tens of jin; the siege equipment Liu Qi brought to Shunchang and to Zhegao was of that kind, together with thunder bombs, scaling ladders and battering rams. On the mechanism: the long-armed counterweight trebuchet was a new instrument of the Mediterranean world of the early twelfth century - Byzantium, the crusader states, the Italian city communes - and it threw its stone by letting a weight hung from the long arm fall, which gave both a longer range and a truer fall. In China that counterweight engine arrived only in the thirteenth century, brought east by the Mongol armies with the craftsmen of Central Asia and appearing under the name of the huihui pao, in which it showed its worth at the siege of Xiangyang between 1268 and 1273; at Shunchang and Zhegao in 1141 there is no trace of it. The position of the weapon on this card in the campaign is therefore the same function and a different mechanism. What it stands for is the logic of stone-throwing siegecraft - the arc over the head of the wall, the stone falling on the engines and the men at the foot of it - and that is exactly what the Song attacking engines were doing at Zhegao; only the piece that actually fired was the traction engine with the transverse arm, while the counterweight machine on this card remained in front of the walls of the Mediterranean world. One further point can be set side by side: a counterweight engine is worked by a handful of men, while the Song traction engine needed a hundred men pulling together, so its interval between shots, its supply of labour and its assault rhythm were all the slower. In engineering terms, whoever sets the rhythm sets the length of the window for a siege. Besides the trebuchet the Song had heavy crossbows and strong bows, longbows, long spears, sabres and rattan shields; for the attack they had scaling ladders, battering rams and ox-hide covered siege gear, and for the defence they kept logs, rolling beams and cheval-de-frise. The Jin attacked with their own engines and ladders and brought masses of cavalry round the walls to strip the countryside and cut off relief. The Song used their horses mainly for scouting, pursuit and dispatch, moved grain by boat on the Huai and by levy from the prefectures along the line, and shifted the heavy pieces - engines, bows, ammunition - on ox carts, mule carts and human backs.
tactics: 順昌的守城是一套以器械與節奏為主的打法。劉錡先在城外掘壕、環城佈拒馬，把金軍的衝車與雲梯逼到弩箭與砲火最有效的距離之內；金軍列陣攻城時，城頭先以強弩齊射封住城根器械的操作位置，再以霹靂砲在結集處發出巨響，用火光與震動擾亂其陣，使騎兵驚潰而步兵進退失據；宋式攻城砲則專打對面最密集之處，把雲梯與衝車連人帶械一起掀翻，把守方最難處理的那一段交給石頭。守住正面之外，他更在意對方的下一步：派斥候繞城偵察、截斷敵軍渡淮的船隻與橋梁、斷其糧道，再用被俘的敵探傳回假情報，聲稱將夜劫大寨，使金軍主帥移營遷就，宋軍趁夜舉火衝營，金軍自相驚擾，營壘連成一片潰散。金軍的戰法以騎兵為主軸：分批輪番攻城以疲敵，再以重兵一舉逼近，同時派騎兵繞城掠糧、遮斷援兵，用兵力優勢把守軍拖垮；攻順昌不克而退屯柘皋，本想重整再攻。柘皋之戰的破法，就是把順昌城頭練出來的節奏搬到野外的營壘上：宋軍追兵攜攻城砲與雲梯逼近，先以砲火覆蓋營柵與望樓，敵騎失去遮蔽，再以步騎火攻合擊，殘敵潰散，宋軍追奔數十里，一路上拆毀並焚燒金軍遺棄的糧車與甲仗。卡面那具配重長臂砲在功能上正是同一件東西——把石頭拋過障礙砸進敵陣——不過中土那時仍用橫臂挽索的砲，兩者在柘皋營前的任務完全一樣。攻防之別說到底在於：守方有牆、有弩、有固定的射界；進攻方必須先用砲火撕開一個口子，才有可能讓步卒貼上城根。
tacticsEn: The defence of Shunchang was a method built on instruments and on timing. Liu Qi first dug ditches outside the walls and set cheval-de-frise around the circuit, so that the battering rams and ladders of the Jin were forced inside the distance at which arrows and stone did their best work. When the Jin closed up for an assault, the wall answered with a massed volley of heavy crossbows that sealed off the ground where the machines were being worked, and then with thunder bombs burst over the massed troops, the flash and the shock breaking their order so that the cavalry bolted and the infantry lost the rhythm of the advance. The Song throwing engines were kept for the densest parts of the enemy line, throwing down ladders and rams together with the men who carried them, handing the hardest minute of the defence over to stone. Beyond holding the front he cared most about what the enemy would do next: scouts went round the walls to watch, the enemy's boats and bridges on the Huai were cut, its supply route broken, and captured enemy scouts were sent back with false intelligence that a night raid on the great camp was coming, so that the Jin commander shifted his camp to suit; the Song then fired the camp in the dark, the Jin host was thrown into confusion, and the camp dissolved into a single rout. The Jin method had cavalry for its axis: successive waves of assault to tire the defenders, then a heavy effort in force, while horsemen rode round the walls to strip the countryside and cut off relief, using their advantage in numbers to exhaust the garrison; when the attack on Shunchang failed they fell back to Zhegao intending to refit and try again. The stroke that broke the Jin at Zhegao was to carry the rhythm worked out on the walls of Shunchang out to a camp in the open field: the pursuing column came on with its throwing engines and its ladders, covered the palisades and the watch towers with stone until the enemy cavalry had no cover, and then infantry and cavalry went in together with fire; what was left broke up, the Song pursued for a number of tens of li, and on the way destroyed and burned the baggage carts and the arms the Jin abandoned. The counterweight trebuchet on this card is the same thing in function - throwing stone over an obstacle and into the enemy's array - except that in mid-twelfth-century China the transverse traction engine was still what was used, and the two had exactly the same task in front of the camp at Zhegao. The difference between attack and defence comes down to this: the defender has a wall, crossbows and fixed fields of fire, while the attacker must first tear an opening with stone before the infantry can reach the foot of the wall at all.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。順昌之役，金軍以十餘萬眾圍城，這是宋廷記敘向來誇大的數目，實際戰兵應遠少於此數；劉錡所部則為一萬餘人，兵力相差數十倍。金兵自紹興十一年（一一四一年）正月圍順昌，攻城數日不能下，退兵三十里；劉錡乘夜焚其營，金軍大潰。柘皋之役緊接其後，劉錡率追兵自順昌向東北直抵柘皋，選銳夜襲並縱火焚營，金軍潰走，宋軍追奔三十餘里，斬獲以萬計，俘馬數千匹，甲仗器械無算。柘皋距順昌約二百里，時值隆冬，淮水沿岸多淺灘泥地，騎兵行動與糧秣運輸都受限制。器械方面，宋代攻城砲發石動輒數十斤，一般可及一百五十至二百步，一次齊射的覆蓋面約數十步，攻守雙方都得按此計算進攻節奏與進攻的時間代價；配重式的長臂砲拋程更遠，但同樣遠不到可以越過營壘直接打中本陣。時間上，從金軍南下到北撤不過數月；紹興十一年十一月《紹興和議》成議，翌年二月在臨安完成換地手續。金廷許諾歸還河南、陝西的唐、鄧、商、秦四州，以淮水為界，歲貢改為銀、絹各二十五萬。劉錡紹興九年（一一三九年）到鎮順昌，紹興十二年（一一四二年）八月卒於潭州，年四十五。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. In the action at Shunchang the Jin surrounded the city with a host numbered at more than a hundred thousand, which is the usual exaggeration of Song reporting and must have been well short of the actual fighting strength; Liu Qi had rather more than ten thousand men, so the odds were tens to one. The Jin besieged Shunchang from the first month of Shaoxing 11 (1141), failed to take it after several days, and withdrew thirty li; Liu Qi fired their camp by night and the host broke. The action at Zhegao followed at once: Liu Qi led his pursuers from Shunchang north-east to Zhegao, chose the picked men for a night assault, put fire to the camp, and the Jin broke up, the Song pursuing for more than thirty li, taking heads by the ten thousand, capturing several thousand horses, and gaining arms and equipment without number. Zhegao lies about two hundred li from Shunchang, and the season was midwinter, with shallows and mud along the Huai that hindered both the movement of cavalry and the transport of grain. As for the instruments, the Song attacking engines threw stones of several tens of jin, generally reached a hundred and fifty to two hundred paces, and a single salvo covered ground of some tens of paces, so that both sides had to compute the rhythm of an assault and its cost in time from those figures; the counterweight trebuchet of the long arm threw further, but not so far as to carry over the camp and strike the enemy in the rear. In time the whole business, from the Jin crossing south to their withdrawal, lasted no more than a few months; in the eleventh month of Shaoxing 11 the Treaty of Shaoxing was agreed, and in the second month of the following year the exchange of territory was carried out at Lin'an. The Jin undertook to return the four circuits of Tang, Deng, Shang and Qin in Henan and Shaanxi, to take the Huai as the boundary, and to remit the annual tribute in silver and silk at twenty-five thousand each. Liu Qi took up his post at Shunchang in the ninth year of Shaoxing (1139) and died of illness at Tanzhou in the eighth month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing (1142), aged forty-five.
cause: 打起來的原因有兩層。第一層是金朝的主動進攻：金人自海陵南侵以來屢次南下，紹興十年（一一四○年）已攻陷河南洛陽，完顏宗弼坐鎮河南，手握河北、山東與河南的兵糧，企圖趁南宋新敗、內部整頓之際再打開淮上局面，逼迫朝廷接受更苛刻的條件。第二層是南宋淮上防線本身的破綻：南渡之後淮南兵力長期不足，淮西一路只靠劉錡所部的孤軍撐住，朝廷對淮東、淮西兩處的指揮、糧餉與援兵都不統一，士氣與補給都要靠將領自己去爭。順昌是淮西北面的門戶，據淮水北岸，控住由河南入淮南的東路大道，金軍要南下必先取順昌；順昌不下，柘皋、滁州一線便無從談起，所以劉錡據城死守並非保守，而是被逼到只能死守的位置。金軍屢攻不克、退屯柘皋，本打算重整再攻，卻正好把宋軍的追擊引到柘皋去；而朝廷內部主和與主戰兩派相持，戰場上的勝敗就直接變成和談桌上的價碼——前線將領每一次勝利都在替朝廷加價，一次失利也會被拿去當成談判的籌碼，柘皋之戰正是在這樣的背景下打成的一場有分量的追擊。
causeEn: There were two layers of cause behind the fighting. The first was the Jin offensive: the Jin had marched south again and again since the campaign of Hailing, had taken Luoyang in Henan in the tenth year of Shaoxing (1140), and Wanyan Zongbi, established in Henan, held the men and the grain of Hebei, Shandong and Henan. He meant to open the Huai front once more while the Song was still smarting from defeat and absorbed in its own reorganisation, and to force the court to accept harder terms. The second layer was the flaw in the Song's own line on the Huai: after the move south the forces in Huainan had been thin for years, the Huaiwest line rested on the lone command of Liu Qi, and the court did not coordinate command, pay or reinforcement between Huai east and Huai west, so that morale and supply had to be fought for by the generals themselves. Shunchang was the door of the north-west Huai: it sat on the north bank and held the eastern road by which an army came from Henan into the south of the river. There was no moving south without taking it, and without Shunchang there could be no question of Zhegao or Chuzhou, which is why Liu Qi's stand was not caution but the only position open to him. The Jin, having failed repeatedly, fell back to Zhegao intending to refit and come again, and it was precisely there that the Song pursuit caught them. Meanwhile the court was split between the advocates of peace and the advocates of war, and the result of a battle on the front became the price on the negotiating table: every victory won by a general added to what the court could ask, and every defeat would have been handed over as a bargaining counter. In that setting the campaign of Zhegao was fought as a pursuit with weight behind it.
impact: 柘皋之戰的直接影響，是把紹興和議的主動權整個換到了宋廷手上。金軍在順昌、柘皋連折兩陣，主力退回淮北，士氣與補給都要重新整理，完顏宗弼無法再往南深入；宋廷則在主戰派手上第一次有了可以攤牌的勝利：紹興十一年（一一四一年）十月金遣韓常、張通古南下議和，十一月《紹興和議》成立，金朝稱臣，歸還河南、陝西部分舊地，以淮水為界，歲貢改為銀絹各二十五萬。從此宋金邊界穩定在淮水南北，雙方維持了百餘年的和平，直到十三世紀末宋室覆亡。對南宋內部而言，這場勝利卻沒有改變權力格局：和議一成，主和派隨即收其兵權，紹興十二年劉錡罷淮西制置使，改知荊州軍府事，後移湖南，八月病卒潭州，年四十五；所向披靡的八字軍就此解散，淮西防務重歸朝廷統一調度，淮南再無可以獨當一面的大將。從軍器史的角度看，這一役也把宋金攻城的樣板定了下來：守城一方以牆體、弩手與霹靂砲構成交叉火網，進攻一方則以攻城砲、雲梯與衝車撕開缺口；砲的射程、覆蓋面與拋射間隔，決定了進攻方能承受多少損失，也決定了守方要在城頭留多少活的器械——這條經驗一直沿用到後來的襄樊之役與宋人對蒙古的攻城戰，而攻城砲由百餘人挽索改為數人配重、令發射間隔與人力補充大為縮短的那一步，正是十三世紀回回砲完成的事。
impactEn: The direct effect of the campaign of Zhegao was to shift the initiative in the peace settlement entirely to the Song side of the table. Having lost two actions in a row, at Shunchang and at Zhegao, the main body of the Jin fell back across the Huai, and both its morale and its supply had to be put in order again; Zongbi could no longer drive south. The Song, for the first time in the hands of the party that wanted war, held a victory that could be played openly: in the tenth month of Shaoxing 11 (1141) the Jin sent Han Chang and Zhang Tonggu south to talk, and in the eleventh month the Treaty of Shaoxing was concluded, the Jin acknowledging vassalage, returning part of the old lands of Henan and Shaanxi, taking the Huai as the frontier, and converting the annual tribute into silver and silk at twenty-five thousand each. From then on the boundary between the two states stood on the Huai, and they kept the peace for more than a century, until the fall of the Song at the end of the thirteenth century. Internally, however, the victory changed nothing in the balance of power. Once the treaty was signed the party of peace moved at once to strip him of his command; in the twelfth year of Shaoxing Liu Qi was removed as Military Commissioner for Huaiwest, made Military Commissioner of Jinghu, and later transferred to Hunan, where he died of illness at Tanzhou in the eighth month, at forty-five; the undefeated Eight-Character Army was disbanded, the defence of the Huaiwest went back into the hands of a single central administration, and the south of the river had no commander of that stature left. From the point of view of the history of weapons, the campaign also fixed the model of Song and Jin siegecraft: the defender built a crossfire of wall, crossbowmen and thunder bomb, while the attacker used throwing engines, scaling ladders and battering rams to tear an opening. The range of the engine, the width of its salvo and the interval between shots decided how much loss the attacker could absorb and how much of his own machinery the defender had to keep alive on the wall; that lesson was used again at Xiangfan and in the Song wars against the Mongols, and the later step in which the attacking engine passed from a hundred men hauling ropes to a few men handling a counterweight - shortening both the interval between shots and the labour needed to supply them - was the work of the huihui pao in the thirteenth century.
result: 結果是宋軍連勝而金軍退回淮北，柘皋一戰成了和談的轉折點。紹興十一年（一一四一年）正月，金軍以十餘萬眾自河南南下，圍順昌；劉錡以一萬餘人的孤軍守城，用霹靂砲震敵、勁弩封鎖器械，數日之後金兵不能下，退三十里，劉錡夜焚其營，金軍大潰。宗弼退屯柘皋重整，劉錡不與喘息，遣追兵攜攻城砲與攻具急進，夜襲縱火，砲火覆蓋營壘，敵營大潰，軍械糧畜委棄無數，宋軍追奔三十餘里而還。柘皋之後金軍沒有再成建制地突破淮水，兩軍在淮南相持；十月金使韓常、張通古到臨安議和，十一月《紹興和議》簽訂，金稱臣、歸地、以淮水為界，翌年二月換地儀式完成，雙方的疆界與歲幣自此固定。劉錡以戰功受封賞，隨即在紹興十二年被罷兵權，改知荊州軍府事，後移湖南，於八月以疾卒於潭州，年四十五。就器械而言，攻城砲在這場戰役中做完了它的兩次任務：守城時壓制敵方攻城器械，追擊時拆毀敵營；卡面那具配重長臂砲雖然沒有出現在順昌與柘皋的城頭，所代表的拋石攻城邏輯卻正是這兩次任務的技術內核，後人記住這場戰役時，記住的不只是劉錡的孤軍夜襲，還有城頭的砲火與柘皋營前的火。
resultEn: The result was a run of Song victories and a Jin withdrawal to the north of the Huai, with the action at Zhegao turning out to be the hinge on which the peace turned. In the first month of Shaoxing 11 (1141) the Jin came south from Henan with a host numbered at more than a hundred thousand and surrounded Shunchang; Liu Qi, with rather more than ten thousand men, held the city, shook the enemy with the thunder bomb, sealed off their siege engines with heavy crossbows, and after several days the Jin could not take it, so they withdrew thirty li, and in the night Liu Qi fired their camp and the host dissolved. Zongbi fell back on Zhegao to refit; Liu Qi gave him no breathing space, sent his pursuers on with the throwing engines and the rest of the siege gear, struck at night with fire, covered the camp with stone, and the enemy camp broke up, leaving arms and cattle and baggage in heaps, the Song pursuing for more than thirty li before turning back. After Zhegao the Jin made no further formed attempt to break across the Huai, and the two armies stood facing each other in the south of the river; in the tenth month the envoys Han Chang and Zhang Tonggu came to Lin'an to talk, in the eleventh month the Treaty of Shaoxing was signed, the Jin acknowledging vassalage, returning land and taking the Huai as the frontier, and in the second month of the following year the exchange of territory was completed and the frontier and the tribute were fixed for good. Liu Qi was rewarded for the victory, and then in the twelfth year of Shaoxing was stripped of his command, made Military Commissioner of Jinghu, and later transferred to Hunan, where he died of illness in the eighth month at Tanzhou, aged forty-five. As for the instruments, the attacking engines completed the two tasks that were assigned to them in this campaign: on the wall they pinned down the enemy's siege engines, on the pursuit they broke the camp; the counterweight trebuchet on this card never appeared on the walls of Shunchang or of Zhegao, but the logic of stone-throwing siegecraft it stands for was the technical core of both tasks, and what later generations remember about the campaign is not only Liu Qi's night attack with a handful of men, but the stone on the wall and the fire before the camp at Zhegao.
